package com.backend.serviceBalance.balances.services;

import com.backend.serviceBalance.accounts.models.Account;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.accounts.repositories.AccountRepository;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.balances.exceptions.IdempotencyConflictException;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.balances.exceptions.InsufficientBalanceException;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.balances.exceptions.TransactionAlreadyCompletedException;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.balances.validators.BalanceValidator;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.configs.CreditRetryPolicy;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.transactions.models.Transaction;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.transactions.models.TransferTransaction;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.transactions.models.enums.TransactionMethod;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.transactions.models.enums.TransactionStatus;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.transactions.repositories.TransactionRepository;
import com.backend.serviceBalance.transactions.repositories.TransferTransactionRepository;
import io.github.resilience4j.circuitbreaker.CircuitBreaker;
import io.github.resilience4j.reactor.circuitbreaker.operator.CircuitBreakerOperator;
import lombok.RequiredArgsConstructor;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.data.r2dbc.core.R2dbcEntityTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.reactive.TransactionalOperator;
import reactor.core.publisher.Mono;
import reactor.util.retry.Retry;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.util.Objects;

@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class BalanceServiceImpl implements BalanceService {

    private final AccountRepository accountRepository;
    private final TransactionRepository transactionRepository;
    private final R2dbcEntityTemplate entityTemplate;
    private final TransactionalOperator transactionalOperator;
    private final BalanceValidator balanceValidator;
    private final CircuitBreaker creditCircuitBreaker;
    private final TransferTransactionRepository transferTransactionRepository;

    @Value("${max-retry}")
    private Long maxRetry;

    @Value("${max-duration-timeout}")
    private Long maxDurationTimeout;

    @Override
    public Mono<Void> credit(String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            balanceValidator.validateCredit(accountId, amount, transactionId);

            return Mono.defer(() -> creditOnce(accountId, amount, transactionId)).timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(maxDurationTimeout)).retryWhen(Retry.backoff(maxRetry, Duration.ofMillis(200)).maxBackoff(Duration.ofSeconds(2)).jitter(0.5).filter(error -> !(error instanceof IdempotencyConflictException) && !(error instanceof TransactionAlreadyCompletedException) && CreditRetryPolicy.isRetryable(error)).onRetryExhaustedThrow((_, signal) -> signal.failure())).transformDeferred(CircuitBreakerOperator.of(creditCircuitBreaker));
        });
    }

    private Mono<Void> creditOnce(String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            Mono<Void> work = accountRepository.findByIdForUpdate(accountId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Account not found: " + accountId))).flatMap(account -> transactionRepository.findByIdForUpdate(transactionId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.defer(() -> createPendingTransaction(accountId, amount, transactionId))).flatMap(transaction -> processCreditTransaction(account, transaction, accountId, amount, transactionId))).then();

            return transactionalOperator.transactional(work);
        });
    }

    private Mono<Transaction> createPendingTransaction(String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return createPendingTransaction(accountId, amount, transactionId, TransactionMethod.CREDIT);
    }

    private Mono<Transaction> createPendingTransaction(String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId, TransactionMethod transactionMethod) {
        LocalDateTime now = LocalDateTime.now();

        Transaction transaction = Transaction.builder().id(transactionId).createdAt(now).updatedAt(now).transactionMethod(transactionMethod).amount(amount).accountId(accountId).transactionStatus(TransactionStatus.PENDING).build();

        return entityTemplate.insert(transaction);
    }

    private Mono<Void> processCreditTransaction(Account account, Transaction transaction, String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        boolean sameOperation = java.util.Objects.equals(transaction.getAccountId(), accountId) && java.util.Objects.equals(transaction.getAmount(), amount) && transaction.getTransactionMethod() == TransactionMethod.CREDIT;

        if (!sameOperation) return Mono.error(new IdempotencyConflictException(transactionId));

        TransactionStatus status = transaction.getTransactionStatus();

        if (status == TransactionStatus.SUCCESS)
            return Mono.error(new TransactionAlreadyCompletedException(transactionId));

        if (status == TransactionStatus.PENDING) return completeCredit(account, transaction).then();

        return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Transaction cannot be credited in status " + status + ": " + transactionId));
    }

    private Mono<Transaction> completeCredit(Account account, Transaction transaction) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            Long currentBalance = account.getBalance();

            if (currentBalance == null || currentBalance < 0)
                return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Account balance is invalid"));

            final long newBalance;

            try {
                newBalance = Math.addExact(currentBalance, transaction.getAmount());
            } catch (ArithmeticException exception) {
                return Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Balance exceeds the supported range", exception));
            }

            account.setBalance(newBalance);

            return accountRepository.save(account).flatMap(_ -> {
                transaction.setTransactionStatus(TransactionStatus.SUCCESS);
                transaction.setUpdatedAt(LocalDateTime.now());

                return transactionRepository.save(transaction);
            });
        });
    }

    @Override
    public Mono<Void> debit(String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            balanceValidator.validateDebit(accountId, amount, transactionId);

            return Mono.defer(() -> debitOnce(accountId, amount, transactionId)).timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(maxDurationTimeout)).retryWhen(Retry.backoff(maxRetry, Duration.ofMillis(200)).maxBackoff(Duration.ofSeconds(2)).jitter(0.5).filter(error -> !(error instanceof IdempotencyConflictException) && !(error instanceof TransactionAlreadyCompletedException) && !(error instanceof InsufficientBalanceException) && CreditRetryPolicy.isRetryable(error)).onRetryExhaustedThrow((_, signal) -> signal.failure())).transformDeferred(CircuitBreakerOperator.of(creditCircuitBreaker));
        });
    }

    private Mono<Void> debitOnce(String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            Mono<Void> work = accountRepository.findByIdForUpdate(accountId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Account not found: " + accountId))).flatMap(account -> transactionRepository.findByIdForUpdate(transactionId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.defer(() -> createPendingTransaction(accountId, amount, transactionId, TransactionMethod.DEBIT))).flatMap(transaction -> processDebitTransaction(account, transaction, accountId, amount, transactionId))).then();

            return transactionalOperator.transactional(work);
        });
    }

    private Mono<Void> processDebitTransaction(Account account, Transaction transaction, String accountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        boolean sameOperation = java.util.Objects.equals(transaction.getAccountId(), accountId) && java.util.Objects.equals(transaction.getAmount(), amount) && transaction.getTransactionMethod() == TransactionMethod.DEBIT;

        if (!sameOperation) return Mono.error(new IdempotencyConflictException(transactionId));

        TransactionStatus status = transaction.getTransactionStatus();

        if (status == TransactionStatus.SUCCESS)
            return Mono.error(new TransactionAlreadyCompletedException(transactionId));

        if (status == TransactionStatus.PENDING) return completeDebit(account, transaction).then();

        return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Transaction cannot be debited in status " + status + ": " + transactionId));
    }

    private Mono<Transaction> completeDebit(Account account, Transaction transaction) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            Long currentBalance = account.getBalance();
            Long amount = transaction.getAmount();

            if (currentBalance == null || currentBalance < 0)
                return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Account balance is invalid"));

            if (amount == null || amount <= 0)
                return Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Amount must be greater than zero"));

            if (amount > currentBalance)
                return Mono.error(new InsufficientBalanceException(account.getId(), currentBalance, amount));

            account.setBalance(currentBalance - amount);

            return accountRepository.save(account).flatMap(_ -> {
                transaction.setTransactionStatus(TransactionStatus.SUCCESS);
                transaction.setUpdatedAt(LocalDateTime.now());

                return transactionRepository.save(transaction);
            });
        });
    }

    @Override
    public Mono<Void> transfer(String sourceAccountId, String destinationAccountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            balanceValidator.validateTransfer(sourceAccountId, destinationAccountId, amount, transactionId);

            return Mono.defer(() -> transferOnce(sourceAccountId, destinationAccountId, amount, transactionId)).timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(maxDurationTimeout)).retryWhen(Retry.backoff(maxRetry, Duration.ofMillis(200)).maxBackoff(Duration.ofSeconds(2)).jitter(0.5).filter(error -> !(error instanceof IdempotencyConflictException) && !(error instanceof TransactionAlreadyCompletedException) && !(error instanceof InsufficientBalanceException) && !(error instanceof IllegalArgumentException) && CreditRetryPolicy.isRetryable(error)).onRetryExhaustedThrow((_, signal) -> signal.failure())).transformDeferred(CircuitBreakerOperator.of(creditCircuitBreaker));
        });
    }

    private Mono<Void> transferOnce(String sourceAccountId, String destinationAccountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            boolean sourceFirst = sourceAccountId.compareTo(destinationAccountId) < 0;

            String firstId = sourceFirst ? sourceAccountId : destinationAccountId;

            String secondId = sourceFirst ? destinationAccountId : sourceAccountId;

            Mono<Void> work = lockTransferAccount(firstId, sourceAccountId).flatMap(first -> lockTransferAccount(secondId, sourceAccountId).flatMap(second -> {
                Account source = sourceFirst ? first : second;

                Account destination = sourceFirst ? second : first;

                return transferTransactionRepository.findByIdForUpdate(transactionId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.defer(() -> createPendingTransfer(sourceAccountId, destinationAccountId, amount, transactionId))).flatMap(transaction -> processTransferTransaction(source, destination, transaction, sourceAccountId, destinationAccountId, amount, transactionId));
            })).then();

            return transactionalOperator.transactional(work);
        });
    }

    private Mono<Account> lockTransferAccount(String accountId, String sourceAccountId) {
        String role = accountId.equals(sourceAccountId) ? "Source" : "Destination";

        return accountRepository.findByIdForUpdate(accountId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException(role + " account not found: " + accountId)));
    }

    private Mono<TransferTransaction> createPendingTransfer(String sourceAccountId, String destinationAccountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        LocalDateTime now = LocalDateTime.now();

        TransferTransaction transaction = TransferTransaction.builder().id(transactionId).sourceAccountId(sourceAccountId).destinationAccountId(destinationAccountId).amount(amount).transactionStatus(TransactionStatus.PENDING).createdAt(now).updatedAt(now).build();

        return entityTemplate.insert(transaction);
    }

    private Mono<Void> processTransferTransaction(Account source, Account destination, TransferTransaction transaction, String sourceAccountId, String destinationAccountId, Long amount, String transactionId) {
        boolean sameOperation = Objects.equals(transaction.getSourceAccountId(), sourceAccountId) && Objects.equals(transaction.getDestinationAccountId(), destinationAccountId) && Objects.equals(transaction.getAmount(), amount);

        if (!sameOperation) return Mono.error(new IdempotencyConflictException(transactionId));

        TransactionStatus status = transaction.getTransactionStatus();

        if (status == TransactionStatus.SUCCESS)
            return Mono.error(new TransactionAlreadyCompletedException(transactionId));

        if (status != TransactionStatus.PENDING)
            return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Transaction cannot be transferred in status " + status + ": " + transactionId));

        return completeTransfer(source, destination, transaction);
    }

    private Mono<Void> completeTransfer(Account source, Account destination, TransferTransaction transaction) {
        return Mono.defer(() -> {
            Long sourceBalance = source.getBalance();
            Long destinationBalance = destination.getBalance();
            Long amount = transaction.getAmount();

            if (sourceBalance == null || sourceBalance < 0)
                return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Source account balance is invalid"));

            if (destinationBalance == null || destinationBalance < 0)
                return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Destination account balance is invalid"));

            if (amount == null || amount <= 0)
                return Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Amount must be greater than zero"));

            if (amount > sourceBalance)
                return Mono.error(new InsufficientBalanceException(source.getId(), sourceBalance, amount));

            final long newDestinationBalance;

            try {
                newDestinationBalance = Math.addExact(destinationBalance, amount);
            } catch (ArithmeticException exception) {
                return Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Destination balance exceeds the supported range", exception));
            }

            source.setBalance(sourceBalance - amount);
            destination.setBalance(newDestinationBalance);

            return accountRepository.save(source).then(accountRepository.save(destination)).then(Mono.defer(() -> transferTransactionRepository.updateTransferTransactionStatus(transaction.getId(), TransactionStatus.SUCCESS))).flatMap(updatedRows -> {
                if (updatedRows != 1)
                    return Mono.error(new IllegalStateException("Expected to update one transfer transaction, " + "but updated " + updatedRows + ": " + transaction.getId()));

                return Mono.empty();
            });
        });
    }

    @Override
    public Mono<Long> getBalance(String accountId) {
        return accountRepository.findBalanceByAccountId(accountId).switchIfEmpty(Mono.error(new IllegalArgumentException("Account not found or balance is null: " + accountId)));
    }
}

با این کد، می‌توانیم README را دقیق‌تر و بر اساس پیاده‌سازی واقعی بنویسیم.

**یک اصلاح مهم:** روش کنترل هم‌زمانی که در این کد دیده می‌شود **Pessimistic Row-Level Locking** با `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` است، نه **Atomic Conditional Update**. دستور تغییر وضعیت هم فقط بر اساس `id` شرط دارد؛ شرطی مثل `transaction_status = 'PENDING'` ندارد. البته به‌دلیل قفل رکورد در تراکنش، این الزاماً اشکال نیست.

همچنین:
- استفاده از **R2DBC** و **TransactionalOperator** مشخص است.
- retry با backoff و jitter پیاده‌سازی شده؛ نوع خطاهای قابل retry به `CreditRetryPolicy` بستگی دارد.
- درخواست‌های متفاوت روی یک حساب می‌توانند به‌ترتیب موفق شوند؛ لزوماً فقط یکی موفق و بقیه `409` نمی‌شوند.
- نگاشت استثناها به `409` در این کد دیده نمی‌شود؛ باید در exception handler تعریف شده باشد.
- برای تضمین جلوگیری از ایجاد رکورد تکراری، `id` باید در دیتابیس **Primary Key یا UNIQUE** باشد.

این بخش را جایگزین بخش پرسش‌وپاسخ قبلی README کن:

```markdown
## Architecture and Design Decisions

### Technologies

#### Which technologies are used?

Service Balance uses:

- **Java and Spring Boot** for backend development.
- **Spring WebFlux and Project Reactor** for reactive request processing.
- **Spring Data R2DBC** for reactive database access.
- **PostgreSQL** for persistent storage, transactions, and row-level locking.
- **Docker** for packaging and simplifying deployment.
- **Resilience4j** for circuit breaker support.
- **Reactor Retry** for configurable retries with exponential backoff and jitter.

#### Why were these technologies selected?

**Docker** simplifies application setup by packaging the application and its dependencies into a consistent environment. Users still need a compatible container runtime, but do not need to install every application dependency individually.

**PostgreSQL** provides:

- Persistent storage for accounts and transactions.
- Database transactions with commit and rollback.
- Row-level locking for concurrent balance updates.
- Data integrity through primary keys, unique constraints, and other SQL constraints.

**Reactive Spring and R2DBC** support asynchronous, non-blocking I/O across the HTTP and database layers.

Reactive execution does not necessarily mean multithreaded execution. Its main advantage for this application is handling I/O without blocking a thread while waiting for completion.

#### What trade-offs do these technologies introduce?

- Database development and maintenance require basic SQL knowledge.
- Docker requires a supported container runtime; some environments require virtualization support.
- Reactive code introduces additional complexity in debugging and transaction management.
- Row-level locking protects data consistency but can increase waiting time under contention.
- Retries improve resilience to transient failures but can increase response latency and database load.

## Architecture

### What is the overall solution structure?

Service Balance follows a layered reactive architecture:

HTTP Client
    → Controller
    → Service and Validator
    → Reactive Repository / R2dbcEntityTemplate
    → PostgreSQL

Database-changing workflows are wrapped in a reactive transaction using
`TransactionalOperator`.

### What are the main system components?

- **Controllers:** Receive HTTP requests and return API responses.
- **Validators:** Validate operation inputs and business constraints.
- **Services:** Implement credit, debit, transfer, and balance retrieval workflows.
- **Repositories:** Read and update account and transaction data.
- **R2dbcEntityTemplate:** Inserts new transaction records.
- **TransactionalOperator:** Defines reactive database transaction boundaries.
- **Retry policy:** Determines which failures can be retried.
- **Circuit breaker:** Limits execution when the configured breaker is open.
- **PostgreSQL:** Stores data and provides transaction and locking guarantees.

## Same-Account Transfers

### What happens when the source and destination accounts are the same?

Same-account transfers are rejected by the transfer validation rule.

No balance changes should be performed for an invalid request.

This follows the expected business rule for bank-style transfers: the source and destination accounts must be different.

The HTTP status and response body depend on the application's exception-handling configuration.

## Concurrency

### How is concurrent data consistency ensured?

The implementation uses **pessimistic row-level locking**:

SELECT *
FROM accounts
WHERE id = :accountId
FOR UPDATE

Account rows are locked before their balances are checked or updated.

Existing transaction records are also retrieved using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`.

These operations run inside a database transaction managed by
`TransactionalOperator`. PostgreSQL holds the row locks until the transaction ends.

This protects the read-check-update workflow across concurrent requests and application instances, provided all competing balance-writing paths follow a compatible locking strategy.

The implementation does not rely on Java-level synchronization or thread-blocking calls for data consistency.

### Why was this approach selected?

Row-level locking prevents concurrent operations from modifying the same account based on an outdated balance.

It makes balance validation and subsequent updates consistent within the database transaction.

Duplicate execution is addressed separately through transaction identifiers, operation matching, status checks, and transaction-record locking.

### What happens when concurrent operations target the same account?

Requests targeting the same locked account generally wait for the current transaction to finish.

After acquiring the lock, each request reads the current account state and continues validation.

Therefore:

- Multiple distinct valid operations may succeed sequentially.
- A debit may fail if an earlier operation leaves insufficient balance.
- Repeated execution of a completed transaction is rejected.
- Lock-related transient failures may be retried if classified as retryable.

Concurrency alone does not imply that all but one request receive `409 Conflict`. HTTP error statuses are determined by the exception-handling layer.

## Idempotency

### How is repeated execution of a transaction prevented?

The supplied `transactionId` identifies the operation.

During credit, debit, or transfer execution, the service:

1. Locks the relevant account rows.
2. Reads and locks the existing transaction, if present.
3. Creates a `PENDING` transaction if no record exists.
4. Verifies that the stored operation matches the requested operation.
5. Rejects a transaction that is already `SUCCESS`.
6. Applies balance changes and records `SUCCESS` in the same database transaction.

For credit and debit, operation matching checks:

- Account ID
- Amount
- Transaction method

For transfers, operation matching checks:

- Source account ID
- Destination account ID
- Amount

Reusing an existing transaction ID with different operation details raises
`IdempotencyConflictException`.

Repeating a completed transaction raises
`TransactionAlreadyCompletedException`.

This provides duplicate-execution protection rather than replaying the original successful response.

### What happens if the same transaction is received concurrently?

For identical requests affecting the same account rows, row-level locks serialize processing.

Once the first request commits successfully, a later request observes the
`SUCCESS` status and does not apply the balance changes again.

Transaction IDs must also be enforced as primary keys or unique values in the database. This is essential when competing requests attempt to insert the same ID without locking the same account rows.

A missing transaction row cannot be protected by `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; database uniqueness handles competing inserts.

Credit/debit transactions and transfer transactions are stored in separate tables. Global uniqueness across both tables is not established by this service code alone.

## Transfer Atomicity

### How is transfer atomicity guaranteed?

Transfer execution runs inside one reactive database transaction using
`TransactionalOperator`.

The transaction includes:

1. Locking both account rows.
2. Reading or creating the transfer transaction.
3. Validating operation details and transaction status.
4. Checking the source balance.
5. Calculating the destination balance with overflow protection.
6. Debiting the source account.
7. Crediting the destination account.
8. Updating the transfer status to `SUCCESS`.

All database changes commit together.

If an operation fails before successful commit, the transaction is rolled back, preventing a partially completed transfer.

Row-level locks provide concurrency control; the database transaction provides atomicity.

### How are invalid balance operations handled?

The implementation rejects:

- Invalid or negative stored balances.
- Non-positive transaction amounts.
- Debits or transfers exceeding the source balance.
- Credit or destination balance overflow.

Destination balance calculations use `Math.addExact` to detect numeric overflow.

The transfer status update must affect exactly one row. Otherwise, the service raises an error and the transaction is rolled back.

## Deadlocks

### Can deadlocks occur?

Deadlocks remain possible in a database application, particularly when other workflows acquire locks in incompatible orders.

However, this implementation reduces transfer-related deadlock risk by locking accounts in a consistent order.

### How does the implementation reduce deadlock risk?

Before acquiring transfer account locks, the service compares the account IDs and locks them in ascending lexicographic order.

This means opposite-direction transfers between the same accounts acquire their account locks in the same order.

PostgreSQL detects deadlocks and aborts one of the involved transactions.

The retry mechanism can retry such failures if `CreditRetryPolicy` classifies them as retryable.

Consistent account lock ordering reduces risk but is not a guarantee that every possible deadlock is eliminated.

## Retry, Timeout, and Circuit Breaker

### How are transient failures handled?

Credit, debit, and transfer operations use configurable retries with:

- Exponential backoff starting at 200 milliseconds.
- A maximum backoff of 2 seconds.
- Jitter of 0.5.
- A maximum retry count configured through `max-retry`.
- A timeout configured through `max-duration-timeout`.

Each retry starts a new transactional execution attempt.

The exact retryable failure categories are defined by `CreditRetryPolicy`.

### Which failures are not retried?

The retry filters explicitly exclude:

- Idempotency conflicts.
- Already-completed transactions.
- Insufficient balance errors for debit and transfer.
- Illegal argument errors for transfer.

Other failures are retried only if the retry policy accepts them.

### How is the circuit breaker applied?

The credit, debit, and transfer execution pipelines use the configured
`creditCircuitBreaker`.

The circuit breaker wraps the retry pipeline and can reject execution when it is open, according to its configuration.

## HTTP Error Mapping

The service raises domain exceptions for conflicts, completed transactions, insufficient funds, and invalid operations.

The HTTP response status and body are defined by the application's exception handler.

For example, an application may map idempotency conflicts or already-completed transactions to `409 Conflict`, but this mapping must be explicitly implemented.
```

## Assistant

دقیقاً در کوئری‌های **`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`** استفاده شده است. این دستور به PostgreSQL می‌گوید ردیف خوانده‌شده را برای تغییرات قفل کند.

### ۱. قفل رکورد حساب در `AccountRepository`

```java
@Query("""
    SELECT *
    FROM accounts
    WHERE id = :accountId
    FOR UPDATE
    """)
Mono<Account> findByIdForUpdate(@Param("accountId") String accountId);
```

این متد در عملیات `creditOnce` و `debitOnce`، **قبل از خواندن و تغییر موجودی حساب** فراخوانی می‌شود:

```java
accountRepository.findByIdForUpdate(accountId)
```

بنابراین اگر دو درخواست روی یک حساب اجرا شوند، درخواست دوم معمولاً منتظر آزاد شدن قفل درخواست اول می‌ماند و سپس موجودی به‌روز را می‌خواند.

### ۲. قفل هر دو حساب در انتقال

در `transferOnce` ابتدا ترتیب قفل‌کردن حساب‌ها تعیین می‌شود:

```java
boolean sourceFirst = sourceAccountId.compareTo(destinationAccountId) < 0;

String firstId = sourceFirst ? sourceAccountId : destinationAccountId;
String secondId = sourceFirst ? destinationAccountId : sourceAccountId;
```

سپس حساب‌ها به همان ترتیب قفل می‌شوند:

```java
lockTransferAccount(firstId, sourceAccountId)
    .flatMap(first ->
        lockTransferAccount(secondId, sourceAccountId)
        // ادامه عملیات
    );
```

متد `lockTransferAccount` هم همان کوئری `FOR UPDATE` را اجرا می‌کند:

```java
return accountRepository.findByIdForUpdate(accountId)
    .switchIfEmpty(...);
```

**ترتیب ثابت قفل‌ها** احتمال deadlock در انتقال‌های معکوس، مثل `A → B` و `B → A`، را کاهش می‌دهد.

### ۳. قفل رکورد تراکنش

در هر دو Repository تراکنش نیز استفاده شده:

```java
// TransactionRepository
SELECT *
FROM transactions
WHERE id = :transactionId
FOR UPDATE
```

```java
// TransferTransactionRepository
SELECT *
FROM transfer_transactions
WHERE id = :transactionId
FOR UPDATE
```

این قفل‌ها هنگام بررسی وضعیت و اجرای **تراکنش موجود** مانع تغییر هم‌زمان همان رکورد می‌شوند. اگر رکورد هنوز وجود نداشته باشد، این کوئری چیزی را قفل نمی‌کند؛ آنجا unique constraint یا primary key برای جلوگیری از درج تکراری ضروری است.

### ۴. قفل‌ها داخل تراکنش نگه داشته می‌شوند

در `creditOnce`، `debitOnce` و `transferOnce` این خط وجود دارد:

```java
return transactionalOperator.transactional(work);
```

با فرض پیکربندی صحیح transaction manager و اتصال R2DBC، قفل‌ها تا **commit یا rollback** همان تراکنش باقی می‌مانند؛ نه فقط تا پایان اجرای `SELECT`.

**پس نام دقیق راهکار تو این است:**

> **Pessimistic concurrency control using PostgreSQL row-level locks (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) within reactive database transactions.**

یعنی **قفل روی ردیف‌های دیتابیس**، نه روی خود Repository یا threadهای جاوا.
